Terrain Generator: heightfields built with nodes

Stable Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-21

Build heightfields from a node graph and place them as engine terrain with ground, rock, dirt and mud splat layers.

The Terrain tab (View menu, next to Nature and Water) builds landscapes from a node graph and places them in the scene as an engine terrain with ground, rock, dirt and mud splat layers. It is the last of the generators (material, texture, nature, water, terrain) and borrows its shape from node-based terrain tools: a graph of sources, shapers, masks and erosion ending in an Output.

The reference/nerthus folder (MIT, a Rust terrain generator of ~100k lines and 25 node families) served as the map of what a complete tool needs. Nothing was copied; the nodes here are our own implementations of well-known techniques (gradient noise, ridged multifractals, Voronoi, terracing, thermal and particle-based hydraulic erosion), sized to what the engine can use today.

1. How a graph works#

The graph carries one kind of data, a field: a square grid of 0..1 values that is either a height map or a mask. Every pattern is defined on the unit square, so the live 129 x 129 preview and the 513 x 513 result show the same landscape. Everything is deterministic for the seeds.

Category Nodes
Sources Perlin (fBm), Ridged (multifractal crests), Voronoi (cells, distance, edges, cracks), Mountain (a massif with ridges), Island (radial mask with noisy shore), Gradient, Constant
Modifiers Levels, Terrace, Stratify (tilted sedimentary layers), Warp (domain warp), Blur, Invert
Derive Slope (steepness mask), Height Range (mask of a height band)
Combine Combine (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Maximum, Minimum, Blend, Screen, Difference, with an optional mask)
Simulate Thermal Erosion (talus slumping), Hydraulic Erosion (droplets carrying sediment; also outputs Wear and Deposit masks)
Output Output: size X/Z, max height, resolution (129/257/513), sea level, beach width, rock slope, bare-rock line; optional Wear and Deposit inputs (from Hydraulic Erosion) become masks

2. The Output node and the splat layers#

The Output turns the final height into the engine terrain and computes the four splat layers from the terrain itself:

Layer Where
0 ground (grass, moss) everywhere that is not rock, beach or underwater
1 rock slopes steeper than Rock above slope (real rise over run from the size and max height) and heights above Bare rock above
2 dirt the beach band just above the sea level
3 mud below the sea level

Weights are normalised to sum to one; the engine resamples them to its splat map. The sea level is only a height used for the layers and the preview: place a Water body at that height (the tab reports it in metres).

3. Presets#

Group Presets
Gentle Rolling Hills
Mountains Alpine Range, Highland Lake
Coast Volcanic Island, Archipelago
Arid Badlands

Each is an ordinary graph you can open and edit. Tests check that every preset builds a valid terrain (values in range, real relief, splat weights summing to one), that thermal erosion softens the surface while conserving material, that hydraulic erosion is deterministic and produces wear and deposit masks, that the same graph at two resolutions shows the same landscape, and that seeds change the result.

4. Engine side (C ABI v8)#

  • CaffeineTerrain (POD) with caffeine_session_set_terrain(entity, terrain, heights, splat_rgba), caffeine_session_terrain and caffeine_session_terrain_height. Heights are 0..1 and scaled by the max height; the optional splat bytes are resampled to the splat map. The Rust doppio-engine crate wraps them as Terrain and Engine::set_terrain/terrain/terrain_height.
  • The session now syncs terrain meshes before rendering (it did not, so a terrain never drew in the editor) and gives the entity the mesh components the renderer looks for.
  • The terrain mesh is centred on its entity; terrain_height(x, z) measures from the corner, and so do the mask reads.
  • Placing is one undo step, selects the entity and reports the sea level; Export writes Terrain/<name>.generator.terrain (a recipe wrapping the CAFTERRAIN1 / TERRAINGRAPH1 text) and a 16-bit height map PNG for other tools.

Masks (C ABI v15)#

Placing a terrain sends the engine more than a height and a splat map: it sends masks, named 0..1 fields that scatter, the biome table and (later) the shaders read to place things by what the terrain is.

Mask Made by Meaning
height engine, from the heightfield normalised height
slope engine angle from the horizontal, 0 flat .. 1 = 90 degrees
curvature engine 0.5 on flat ground, towards 1 in a valley, towards 0 on a ridge (+-0.125 per metre is the full range)
flow graph (Output node) D8 flow accumulation: how much of the terrain drains through a texel, log-scaled
wetness graph steady drainage that is not steep, plus everything at or below the sea level
wear, deposit graph, when wired what hydraulic erosion took and left; the Output node has two optional inputs for them (the presets with erosion wire them)

The built-ins cost nothing: the engine computes them from the heightfield on demand. The stored ones are 8 bits per texel on the heightfield's grid (a mask is a weight, not a height), up to 16 per terrain, saved with the terrain file (version 3; a terrain without masks is still written as version 2 so older readers open it).

  • caffeine_session_set_terrain_mask(entity, name, res_x, res_z, bytes) (NULL bytes removes it), terrain_mask_count, terrain_mask_at (name, grid, built-in), terrain_mask(entity, name, x, z) for one point and terrain_mask_rect(entity, name, x0, z0, x1, z1, w, h, out) to resample a rectangle. Coordinates are metres from the terrain's corner, like terrain_height; outside the terrain reads the nearest edge.
  • caffeine_session_terrain_normal(entity, x, z): the unit surface normal.
  • The Rust crate wraps them: Engine::set_terrain_mask, remove_terrain_mask, terrain_masks, terrain_mask, terrain_mask_rect, terrain_normal.

The biome table#

terrain/TerrainBiome turns masks into the 0..1 density of each scatter class: a class density is base x a product of terms, each term a trapezoid over one mask. It is plain text and plugs straight into the scatter module's density callback:

text
class 2 base 0.9            # trees: gentle, dry, above the beach
  slope     0.00 0.00 0.15 0.35
  wetness   0.00 0.00 0.30 0.60
  height    0.22 0.28 1.00 1.00
class 1 base 1              # rocks: steep ground
  slope     0.30 0.45 1.00 1.00

A class without a rule has density 1; a term that names a mask the terrain does not have gives 0 (nothing is placed rather than everywhere) and missingMasks lists those names. Tested end to end: scattered trees never land on steep or wet ground and rocks only on the ridge. The editor reads a table through the scatter plan below; a World tab that edits tables visually is phase 6 of the world roadmap.

Scatter on a terrain (C ABI v16)#

Scene > Scatter on Terrain (id editor.menu.scene.scatter_terrain), or the Scatter button in this tab's toolbar (next to Place in scene; it scatters the selected terrain, else the one you placed last), places a whole plan of vegetation and rocks on the selected terrain in one undo step. The plan is a project text file, Scatter/default.scatter, written from a built-in plan the first time; edit it and run the action again. A class line says what (shape, size, spacing, scale, tilt, sink, tint, variants, Micromesh), and the lines under it are the biome terms that say where, the same trapezoids as above:

text
seed 7
class 1 name boulder primitive sphere color 0.45 0.43 0.40 size 1.6 1.1 1.4 cell 16 radius 2.2 density 0.9 priority 30 scale 0.7 1.6 tilt 0.8 sink 0.3 micromesh on
  slope 0.30 0.45 1.00 1.00
class 2 name pine primitive cone color 0.12 0.32 0.15 size 1.8 6 1.8 cell 8 radius 2.4 density 0.85 priority 20 scale 0.8 1.4 tilt 0.1 tint 0.1
  slope   0.00 0.00 0.15 0.35
  wetness 0.00 0.00 0.30 0.60
  height  0.12 0.20 0.70 0.85

Edit scatter plan (toolbar) opens the plan in the script editor. A class can also be a composite: indented part mesh <path> [slots a.mat;b.mat] [micromesh on|off] [cutout on|off] lines make every instance an empty entity with one child per part (a generated tree is a solid and a foliage mesh); the Nature tab's Add to scatter plan writes them for you.

A shape is primitive <cube|sphere|cone|cylinder|capsule|pyramid|torus> or mesh <path> (a {v} in the path is the variant number, so a .nature rock set scatters as variants); material <path> and color r g b set the look. The plan is validated before anything is placed: a bad line or a biome term for a mask the terrain does not have reports an error in the status bar and changes nothing.

What happens underneath:

  • scatterTerrain (src/caffeine/scatter/TerrainScatter) runs the deterministic scatter core over a region of the terrain with its height, normal and the biome density. The result depends only on the seed, the plan and the terrain, not on the chunk size: the two halves of a region add up to the whole. It stops at maxInstances and reports the total, so the status line tells you when the plan was cut (default 5 000 in the editor; raise it with max_instances).
  • caffeine_session_scatter_terrain(session, entity, seed, classes, class_count, biome_text, region, out, capacity, out_total) returns each instance's world position, up (the terrain normal), Euler rotation in degrees, scale, tint and variant. capacity 0 only counts. caffeine_biome_check(text, error, size) validates a table. The Rust crate wraps them as Engine::scatter_terrain and biome_check.
  • Doppio creates a holder entity Scatter <plan name> and one child per instance with Mesh Filter, Mesh Renderer (material, tint = class colour x instance tint, Micromesh) and the position, rotation and scale from the engine. Same seed and plan, same placement.
  • Limits: every instance is an entity, so thousands are slow to edit (the instanced and Micromesh draw paths handle them, per-chunk instance buffers are phase 4); the plan is global to the terrain (no painted regions yet); rocks use a single height sample at the instance centre.

5. Limits and roadmap#

This is the first slice of a tool that is far larger elsewhere (the reference has ~25 node families). Honest status:

  • Node coverage. 19 nodes against the reference's hundreds. Missing families, roughly in the order they matter: rivers and lakes (flow routing, carving, water masks), snow and glaciers, sediment and scree simulations, rock detail (outcrops, shattered stone, sandstone), cartography (contours, hillshade), vegetation and object scattering from masks, vector masks (splines, roads), file input (import heightmaps and meshes), and a colorize stage that paints a colour map from palettes and masks.
  • Fidelity. The erosion is a compact particle model, not a production solver: it carves believable gullies and deposits but does not match dedicated tools on large, long-running simulations; it runs on the CPU at up to 513 x 513. The engine itself accepts terrains up to 4097 x 4097 and its chunked LOD draws them (a 1025 x 1025 terrain submits about 0.84 M of its 2.1 M triangles in about 410 draws; see the benchmark set in micromeshes.md); what is missing is a generator output above 513 and tiling or streaming of anything larger than one heightfield.
  • Splat textures. The four layers use the terrain component's layer texture paths (defaults point at the hdr-assets-texture ground sets). In a project without them the terrain draws dark; choosing the layer textures from the tab is next. There is no snow layer (the engine has four), so mountains show rock, not snow.
  • Masks to the engine. Only the four splat layers reach the engine. Wear, deposit and flow masks stay in the graph; exporting masks as images and driving vegetation scatter from them is not done.
  • A process-wide cache. The engine's terrain cache is a singleton keyed by entity id and a session's teardown clears it, so two engine sessions in one process must not build terrains at the same time (the engine tests take a lock for this). A per-session cache is the clean fix.
  • One output. One terrain per graph; no tiling or multi-terrain export, no build/export queue.
  • Preview. The 3D preview is a software render of the splat colours and sea plane with a 1.4x vertical exaggeration; the engine's lighting, shadows and textures differ.
  • Water. The sea level is a number, not a water body; the Water tab places the surface separately.
  • Tuning. Preset relief and sea levels were tuned against the software preview and a single engine render; expect to adjust them (max height, sea, rock slope) per project.

World-level plan (masks to the engine, scatter, chunk streaming): see photoreal-world-roadmap.md.

6. Agents and scripting#

The tab is a pane like the others (editor.pane.terrain_generator, terraingen.* ids). Headless: fixture terrain (reset takes a preset, e.g. Badlands); no engine is needed for the graph and preview. Placement and rendering are covered by engine-backed tests.

The toolbar buttons are the MCP actions terrain_scatter and terrain_edit_scatter_plan (and the Nature tab's nature_add_to_scatter). Agents place a scatter with the MCP action scatter_on_terrain (plan_text or plan_file, seed, max_instances, terrain_id); it sends the same message as the menu, so it is one undo step too. Tests: scatter_on_terrain_places_the_plan_by_the_terrains_masks (engine-backed).

7. Regenerating the images#

bash
./scripts/capture-terrain-docs.sh                                              # the tab (headless, no engine)
./scripts/render-terrain-mask-docs.sh                                          # the mask sheet (engine renders and reads back every mask)
DOPPIO_TERRAIN_DUMP=/tmp/terrain cargo test -p doppio-ui --lib terrain_presets_dump   # preview of every preset
DOPPIO_TERRAIN_DUMP=/tmp/terrain cargo test -p doppio-ui --lib placing_a_terrain      # engine render of Alpine Range

The layers are project materials#

The Output node holds four material slots (ground, rock, dirt, mud). Applying a preset, or placing, fills empty slots by baking a material-library picture into Terrain/Layers/<layer>.png and writing a Terrain/Layers/<layer>.mat whose albedo map is that picture. The slot holds the .mat; placing paints the engine's Splat Layer Paths 1..4 with each material's albedo map. A slot that already has a path, or a file that already exists, is never touched: repaint the PNG, edit the .mat, or pick another material from the node's list. A slot holding a plain picture (older graphs) still works.

Limit: the engine's splat shader blends the four albedo pictures only. Normal, roughness and the other .mat channels are stored in the file but not used for terrain layers yet; that needs a shader change.

Old .terrain-graph files load as before; their empty slots are filled the next time you apply or place.

Using it in a world#

The World Composer starts from a terrain recipe: its terrain line names a *.generator.terrain, the editor bakes it, and the composition's classes read its masks (slope, height, curvature, flow, wetness, ...) with the same biome terms as the table above. The composer adds one mask of its own, water_distance, and a river with carve lowers the baked heightfield before any class reads it.
